text: Weather balloon recovered 1967 Australia contained no instruments, only handwritten letter dated 1823 asking if the great silence had ended yet. Paper was manufactured in 1994.

Crossreference error: Municipal census, Florence 1398, lists 847 residents named Giovanni but only 23 birth records exist. The remaining 824 claim they arrived with the bells but no bells were installed that year.

Librarian's report, Ptolemaic Alexandria 47 BCE: Scroll discovered in ruins describes combustion engine principles with hieroglyphic diagrams. Papyrus carbondates to correct era. Knowledge appears indigenous, not anachronistic.
Medical examiner's notes, Prague 1891: Deceased's stomach contents included seeds from plants extinct for 200 million years. Seeds were still viable. Cause of death listed as temporal indigestion.
Crossreference: Property deed for Manhattan lot, 1664, includes mineral rights to all substances yet undreamed. Recent survey found uranium deposits shaped like the seller's signature.

Interrogation transcript, Salem 1693: Accused witch confessed to flying but claimed she had a pilot's license. Document includes photocopy of FAA certification dated 1987. Court accepted this as evidence of innocence.

Archaeological report: Roman villa excavation, 79 CE Pompeii, ash layer preserved room containing 847 identical clay amphorae. Each amphora holds different vintage of wine that won't be invented until 1847. All wines perfectly aged.

Census records, Lisbon 1755: Three households reported identical family members who cast no shadows. Tax assessor noted shadowabsence reduced property values by 40. Earthquake destroyed records. Families survived unharmed.

Geological survey, Pleistocene epoch, 2.1 million BCE: Sediment core contains fossilized library card embedded in mammoth tusk. Card shows overdue book from 1973. Late fees compound daily across epochs.

Performance review, London Theatre Royal, October 1782: Actor forgot lines during Hamlet soliloquy, began reciting dialogue from play that wouldn't be written until 1953. Audience applauded. Playwright still unborn.

Digital archaeology, ARPANET node logs 1972: User timekeeper99 accessed system three years before username protocols existed. Login duration: negative 47 minutes. Session included file transfer to server that won't be built until 1979.

Inventory discrepancy, Vatican Library 1503: Illuminated manuscript depicts Battle of Waterloo with historically accurate detail. Waterloo occurs in 1815. Manuscript vellum carbondated to 1388. Illuminator died of plague in 1502.

Architectural survey, Babylon 1750 BCE: Ziggurat contains elevator shaft with bronze call buttons. Cuneiform inscription reads Floor 7: Hanging Gardens. Gardens won't exist for 600 years. Shaft descends infinitely downward.
Autopsy report, County Coroner 1936: Subject died from exposure to element not discovered until 1940. Cause of death listed as acute berkelium poisoning. Element occurs naturally nowhere on Earth.
